newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - July 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - July 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pakistan's Chief Justice Sajjad Ali Shah has taken suo moto notice of increased violence and killings in Karachi and has asked the provincial government to explain its position.
- Pakistan and Iran agreed to coordinate efforts in using their influences on Taleban and northern alliance leaders for peaceful settlement of Afghan problem.
- The government is not considering any major devaluation of Pakistani rupee against the dollar to boost exports, Commerce Minister Ishaq Dar said.
- Former commerce minister Ahmed Mukhtar said trade policy announced on Wednesday would benefit India because it promoted one-sided trade with the regional rival.

- The U.S. Senate unanimously adopted an amendment that would clear the way for resumption of military exchanges between Pakistan and the U.S. and provide the vital insurance cover to U.S. investors in Pakistan.
- Muhammad Yaqub, governor of the State (central) Bank of Pakistan hinted that banks could be asked to finance setting up of the proposed banking courts for netting in loan defaulters.
- The business community received the "export-oriented" trade policy with cautious optimism.
- Leading importers and exporters said government target to slash trade deficit by $1.04 billion during fiscal 1997/98 (July-June) was ambitious and unattainable.
- The government of the North West Frontier Province and a U.S. firm Balous signed a memorandum of understanding for $5 million investment in the exploration of gemstones.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan favoured floatation of inflation-indexed bonds.
- Pakistan and Japan will sign three agreements on aid and investment during a four-day visit of the Japanese foreign minister Yuki Aiko this month.
